data.raw_text:
A new research has shown that the world's oldest known human mummies were created by smoke-drying corpses 10,000 years ago in Southeast Asia and China, long before mummification became commonplace in Chile and Egypt. A study of dozens of ancient graves found in China, the Philippines, Laos, Thailand, Malaysia and Indonesia revealed that many skeletons that were found in a tight fetal position were treated by an extended period of smoke-drying over fire before being buried. 

The researchers used X-ray diffraction, a nondestructive technique that allows scientists to investigate the internal microstructure of a material, and infrared spectroscopy to assess whether the bones had been exposed to heat. Many of the skeletons revealed evidence of low-intensity heating and discoloration from soot, rather than evidence of direct combustion such as a cremation. This suggests that a specialized mortuary practice involving the smoking of a corpse was likely practiced widely in pre-farming communities across southern China and Southeast Asia.

Although the deceased individuals the researchers investigated in their study are only bones — with no skin, soft tissue or hair preserved — they consider the remains to be mummies from 4,000 to 12,000 years ago. During this process the skeletons were "hyperflexed,"  meaning the bodies were bound up so the arms and legs could be moved beyond their natural limits as the body decomposed.

Smoke-dried mummies are still being made today in parts of Southeast Asia.

📷 : A modern smoke-dried mummy from the Dani people, Papua, Indonesia. (📷© Hirofumi Matsumura and Hsiao-chun Hung)

#archaeohistories

data.raw_text:
$GRAB Autonomous Shuttle Bus

Singapore Pilot with Autonomous A2Z (A2Z): Launched on July 9, 2025, this six-month trial retrofits a BYD electric mini-bus with A2Z's Level 4 autonomous tech (software, hardware) and Grab's IoT devices for real-time tracking via the Grab app. The 22-seater shuttle connects Grab's One-North HQ to the One-North MRT station over a 3.9 km route, operating 2 hours daily (2-4 PM off-peak) with a safety driver onboard. It features 11 sensors (LiDAR, radar, cameras) for 360° perception and an auto-stop algorithm for safety. Insights will inform Singapore's AV ambitions, with training for Grab drivers as safety operators.

Investment and Partnership with WeRide: In August 2025, Grab made a strategic equity investment in WeRide (NASDAQ: WRD), a global AV leader, to deploy Level 4 robotaxis and autonomous shuttles across Southeast Asia. This builds on Grab's OEM relationships and high utilization rates, aiming to scale fleets for urban mobility. CEO @AnthonyPY_Tan highlighted AVs as a core growth driver, with pilots like food delivery robots on Sentosa Island (using Neolix tech) testing integration.

Regional Expansion Signals: In August 2025, Philippine Secretary of Transportation Vince Dizon rode Grab's shuttle and expressed interest in similar tech for Manila, potentially easing traffic and shortages. Grab's "JustGrab Green" program complements this by promoting EV adoption.
